sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation and shifting the liability on the Insurance Company.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the claimant has sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 11.06.2013 at about 5.30 p.m., near Kela Parkala, Herga Village, on Udupi-Karkala Road between the vehicles i.e., Honda Activa bearing No.KA-47-E-6262 and Tempo bearing No.KA-20-6179.

Therefore, the claimant has filed claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act,
seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
The Tribunal has granted the compensation under various heads as follows:
Sl . No

. Particulars Amount (in.Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 1,00,000.00
2. Medical expenses 43,660.00 3. Loss of amenities 1,00,000.00 4. Loss of earning capacity 20,000.00 during laid up period 5.
Future medical expenses 20,000.00 Total 2,83,660.00 5.
In the present case, the offending vehicle is tempo bearing No.KA-20-6179, which is light motor vehicle having gross vehicle weight of 5300 kgs.
The driver of the tempo has applied for driving license on 06.03.2022 for both transport and non transport.
The accident was caused on 11.06.2013.

The driving license for light motor vehicle (transport) has expired before the accident but the driving Rocky M Pinto vs Jayashekara on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111271232/
2 license to drive the light motor vehicle (non transport) is continued till 30.08.2018.

Therefore, even though the driving license to drive the light motor vehicle (transport) expired before the accident but the light motor vehicle (non transport) is continued even after the accident, therefore, it is only issue having to drive the light motor vehicle (transport and non transport).

The issue is no more res integra in view of the principles of law laid down in the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited, reported in AIR 2017 SC 3668.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the person who is holding driving license to drive the light motor vehicle (non-transport)
is also competent to drive the light motor vehicle (transport).
Hence, on this ground, the Insurance Company cannot be exonerated.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation by indemnifying the owner of the offending vehicle.

6. From the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant had suffered following injuries:
(a) Fracture of right distal redius.
(b) Fracture of right tibial plateau.
(c) Fracture of left III rib.
laceration over right hand.
(e) 2x1 cm abrasion over left elbow.
(f) 5x2x1 cm.
laceration over right leg.
10x4x3 cm. laceration over face.
7. The above said injuries are grievous in nature.
It is observed by the Tribunal that the claimant being the watchman and he is continued in the same job with same salary.
Therefore, there is no disability affecting the future income of the claimant.
Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in awarding the compensation under various heads as above stated except under the heads 'loss of earning during laid up period' and for 'future medical expenses'.
The doctor has stated that the claimant is recovered.
Furthermore, a sum of Rs.1,75,000/- towards future medical expenses is required but there is no substantiation to prove this much of amount is required for future medical expenses.

However, considering the nature of injuries sustained, the claimant is required some more amount towards 'future medical expenses' and also 'during laid up period', the claimant must not have attended the work of watchman at least for a period of five months and that is to compensated.
Therefore, by considering this over all injuries and medical amount expenses, it is just and proper to make enhancement of compensation by awarding another sum of Rs.70,000/-.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for additional sum of Rs.70,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

8. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:

3 ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.871/2013 is hereby modified that the claimant is entitled for additional compensation of Rs.70,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation by indemnifying the owner of the offending vehicle No.KA-20-6179.
iv. The claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 412 days in filing the appeal.
v. Costs made easy.

vi. Draw award accordingly.
